newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Crown seen likely suitor for Sydney casino.
newsitem.headline: Crown seen likely suitor for Sydney casino.

text.p: Analysts on Monday tipped Crown Ltd as a likely buyer of the management contract for Sydney Harbour Casino Ltd (SHC) after Kerry Packer's Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd (PBL) withdrew an offer to buy 85 percent of the contract from Showboat Inc.
"If Showboat are a seller, and you have to assume they are, then Crown are probably one of their better contenders," one Sydney-based analyst said.
Market commentators also speculate that Victorian gambling group, Tabcorp Holdings Ltd, and Sydney-based gaming machine operator AWA Ltd, were also interested parties.
"They (Crown) would be interested if the price were right and if they believed they had some possibility of success. They have talked about a merger before," the Sydney analyst said.
However, on Sunday Showboat said from Las Vegas that it looked forward to retaining its position in the management company and in the ownership of its 24.6 percent stake in SHC.
On Saturday, PBL said it had allowed the A$240 million deal to lapse because of difficulties encountered with the Casino Control Authority (CAA), the regulator of casinos in New South Wales.

Analysts said Crown could find the resources to buy the contract but that the market was keen to see the company prove that its large investment in its new casino generated the returns required to support the investment.
Analyst estimate that Crown has spent up to A$2 billion building its new permanent casino in Melbourne.

"If Crown took over the contract, market reaction would probably be positive for Sydney Harbour Casino but perhaps negative in the short term for Crown," said Kevin Lourey, a dealer at Melbourne broker, Peake Lands Kirwin.
However, securing the Sydney casino managment contract would be likely to be very positive for Crown's shares in the long term, Lourey said.
A spokeswoman for Tabcorp said the company could not comment on potential acquisitions. However, Tabcorp has said it would examine any opportunities in the wagering and gaming business in Australia.
Spokesmen from Crown and AWA were unavailable for comment.
At 2.35 p.m (0335 GMT), Crown shares two cents firmer at A$2.27 while SHC stock was two cents weaker at A$2.14.
